primitives.name: Message Entropy
primitives.verbatim_quote: It turns out that the less probable a message is, the more meaning it carries, which is entirely reasonable from the standpoint of our common sense.1 We ordinarily think of a message as sent from human being to human being.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'discrete random variable representing message symbols', 'p(x_i)': 'probability of symbol x_i, dimensionless', '\\mathcal{H}(X)': 'entropy in bits'}
primitives.assumptions: Messages form a discrete probability distribution; symbols are independent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p(x_i) approaches 0 or 1, entropy diverges or vanishes respectively.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core concept of cybernetics centers on message transmission and control through feedback mechanisms. In GSI, this translates into probabilistic inference where messages carry entropy-weighted information. Each message is a pattern drawn from a set of possibilities, and its meaning emerges from selection among those patterns. As entropy increases, so does the information content—this is fundamental to how GSI decodes signals into actionable beliefs. In GSE, control messages drive behavioral changes in agents, modeled as state transitions governed by feedback functions. These systems must maintain coherence between transmitted signals and resulting actions. The duality lies in the fact that while one party sends a message, another receives and interprets it, forming a closed-loop system. Failure modes include loss of signal integrity due to noise or misinterpretation, leading to incorrect control decisions or belief updates. The mathematical framework ensures robustness against such failures by quantifying uncertainty and optimizing communication efficiency.
